simple: one chip that holds the processor cores and most of the devices a computer needs.
analogy: a whole school in one building, with the boiler room, the library and the classrooms under one roof.
precise: an integrated circuit containing CPU cores, an interconnect, memory controllers, on-chip SRAM and ROM, and many peripheral blocks (UARTs, timers, storage and network controllers), with fixed physical addresses decided by the chip vendor and documented, if at all, in its technical reference manual.
source: C1 of F4-31 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 11.1 "How SoC hardware differs from a PC", 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist" and milestone D8 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html), and the University Authoring Guide's bridge BR-07: the ten-aspect comparison, the checklist order and the D8 acceptance test quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a data file that describes the hardware of one machine: what is there, at which address, and how the parts are connected.
analogy: the building plan the caretaker hands to a new principal.
precise: a tree of nodes with named properties, defined by the Devicetree Specification, passed to the OS in the flattened binary form (DTB) so that the OS can discover devices that cannot be enumerated.
source: D1 of F4-31 (devicetree.org, "Devicetree Specification" (tier 1): chapters "The Devicetree" (standard properties: compatible, reg, #address-cells, #size-cells, ranges, status, phandle), "Device Node Requirements" (/memory, /chosen, /cpus) and "Flattened Devicetree (DTB) Format") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the devicetree packed into one block of bytes that a loader can put in memory.
analogy: the plan folded into an envelope.
precise: a big-endian binary with a 40-byte header (magic 0xd00dfeed, total size, offsets of the structure block, strings block and memory reservation map, version), a structure block of tokens (BEGIN_NODE 1, END_NODE 2, PROP 3, NOP 4, END 9) and a strings block for property names.
source: D1 of F4-31 (devicetree.org, "Devicetree Specification" (tier 1): chapters "The Devicetree" (standard properties: compatible, reg, #address-cells, #size-cells, ranges, status, phandle), "Device Node Requirements" (/memory, /chosen, /cpus) and "Flattened Devicetree (DTB) Format") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: working out which CPU address a device really has when the plan writes its address in the local numbering of a bus.
analogy: room "2.14" in the east wing is "E2.14" from the main entrance.
precise: a reg address is in the address space of the node's parent bus; each ranges entry (child address, parent address, length) maps a window of the child space into the parent space; an empty ranges means identity; a missing ranges means the child space is not memory-mapped from the parent.
source: D1 of F4-31 (devicetree.org, "Devicetree Specification" (tier 1): chapters "The Devicetree" (standard properties: compatible, reg, #address-cells, #size-cells, ranges, status, phandle), "Device Node Requirements" (/memory, /chosen, /cpus) and "Flattened Devicetree (DTB) Format") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number that one node uses to point at another node.
analogy: "see room 8000" written on a door.
precise: a 32-bit value stored in a node's phandle property and quoted in other nodes' properties (clocks, interrupt-parent, resets, pin control) to reference it.
source: D1 of F4-31 (devicetree.org, "Devicetree Specification" (tier 1): chapters "The Devicetree" (standard properties: compatible, reg, #address-cells, #size-cells, ranges, status, phandle), "Device Node Requirements" (/memory, /chosen, /cpus) and "Flattened Devicetree (DTB) Format") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the first program an SoC runs, burned into the chip when it is made.
analogy: the fixed first caretaker at the gate, who never changes and only knows where to find the next person.
precise: read-only code inside the SoC that runs at reset, reads boot-mode pins or fuses, loads the next stage from a boot medium into on-chip SRAM in a vendor-specific format, optionally verifies its signature, and often offers a USB recovery mode.
source: C1 of F4-31 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 11.1 "How SoC hardware differs from a PC", 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist" and milestone D8 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html), and the University Authoring Guide's bridge BR-07: the ten-aspect comparison, the checklist order and the D8 acceptance test quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the big book from a chip vendor that describes every register of every block on the chip.
analogy: the architect's full drawings, not the summary plan.
precise: the vendor's programming documentation for one SoC (address map, clock and reset trees, pin multiplexing, each peripheral's registers), whose public availability ranges from complete to none, depending on the vendor.
source: C1 of F4-31 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 11.1 "How SoC hardware differs from a PC", 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist" and milestone D8 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html), and the University Authoring Guide's bridge BR-07: the ten-aspect comparison, the checklist order and the D8 acceptance test quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: 64 bytes at the very start of an Arm 64-bit kernel file that tell a loader how to place it.
analogy: the label on a delivery box that says "this side up, put it in room 0x80000".
precise: a header with a branch instruction, the text offset, the image size, flags (endianness, page size, placement) and the magic "ARM\x64" at offset 0x38, after the Linux arm64 booting document; QEMU's direct kernel boot recognises it.
source: D2 of F4-31 (The Linux kernel documentation (tier 2), "Booting AArch64 Linux" (the arm64 booting document): image header, placement, register and CPU state at entry) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of programs that run one after another from power-on until your kernel starts.
analogy: the people who open the school in the morning, each handing an envelope to the next.
precise: on Arm SoCs, a boot ROM, a first stage that initialises DRAM, an EL3 runtime (TF-A BL31), an optional secure-world OS (BL32), a normal-world loader (BL33) and the OS, each loaded and optionally verified by the one before.
source: D1 of F4-32 (Trusted Firmware project, "Trusted Firmware-A documentation" (tier 2), especially "Firmware Design" (boot stages BL1, BL2, BL31, BL32, BL33; image loading; entry-point information) and the QEMU platform port) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the open reference firmware for the secure parts of booting an Arm 64-bit chip.
analogy: the caretaker's rule book, used by many schools.
precise: the Trusted Firmware project's implementation of the Arm boot stages BL1 (ROM-like first stage), BL2 (trusted boot loader), BL31 (EL3 runtime with PSCI and the SMC dispatcher), with interfaces to BL32 (secure payload) and BL33 (non-secure firmware).
source: D1 of F4-32 (Trusted Firmware project, "Trusted Firmware-A documentation" (tier 2), especially "Firmware Design" (boot stages BL1, BL2, BL31, BL32, BL33; image loading; entry-point information) and the QEMU platform port) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: firmware that stays in memory after the kernel starts, in the most privileged mode, to do the few things the kernel may not do itself.
analogy: the caretaker who lives in the office all day.
precise: the TF-A stage resident at exception level 3 in secure memory; it owns VBAR_EL3, handles SMC exceptions from lower levels (PSCI, SMCCC services, sometimes SCMI or vendor services) and switches between the secure and non-secure worlds.
source: D1 of F4-32 (Trusted Firmware project, "Trusted Firmware-A documentation" (tier 2), especially "Firmware Design" (boot stages BL1, BL2, BL31, BL32, BL33; image loading; entry-point information) and the QEMU platform port) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the instruction a kernel uses to ask the EL3 firmware for a service.
analogy: a note passed through the office hatch to the caretaker.
precise: an AArch64 instruction that, when permitted by SCR_EL3, takes a synchronous exception to EL3 with exception class 0x17; the SMC Calling Convention defines the function ID in w0, arguments in x1 onwards and results in x0 to x3.
source: D3 of F4-32 (Arm, "SMC Calling Convention" (DEN0028) (tier 1): function ID layout, register usage, NOT_SUPPORTED) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the standard list of power requests an OS can send to firmware: start a CPU, stop a CPU, power off, reset.
analogy: the printed form the teacher fills in for the caretaker.
precise: an Arm specification of firmware functions (PSCI_VERSION, CPU_ON, CPU_OFF, SYSTEM_OFF, SYSTEM_RESET and others) called through SMC or HVC with fixed function IDs, advertised to the OS by a /psci devicetree node or ACPI.
source: D2 of F4-32 (Arm, "Arm Power State Coordination Interface Platform Design Document" (DEN0022) (tier 1): function IDs, PSCI_VERSION, SYSTEM_OFF, SYSTEM_RESET, PSCI_FEATURES, return codes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: small first versions of U-Boot that fit in the chip's on-chip memory and start the DRAM.
analogy: the facilities manager who switches on the heating before anyone else can work.
precise: U-Boot's Secondary and Tertiary Program Loaders: reduced builds that run from on-chip SRAM, initialise clocks and DRAM, and load the next stages (TF-A BL31, OP-TEE, U-Boot proper) into DRAM.
source: D5 of F4-32 (U-Boot project, "The U-Boot Documentation" (tier 2): SPL and TPL, standard boot, booti, the UEFI implementation, devicetree fix-ups) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two separate sets of privileges inside one chip; the normal OS runs in one, trusted firmware in the other.
analogy: the locked wing of the school that teachers cannot enter.
precise: Arm's TrustZone security states; SCR_EL3.NS selects the state of the levels below EL3, and memory and devices can be made accessible only to the secure state.
source: D4 of F4-32 (Arm, "Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile architecture" (tier 1): SCR_EL3, SPSR_EL3, ELR_EL3, VBAR_EL3 and the vector table offsets, exception return and illegal exception returns, ESR_ELx exception classes 0x0E and 0x17, RVBAR_EL3, CNTFRQ_EL0, the Security states) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way to load a program into a board over USB when nothing on its storage works.
analogy: the side gate the old caretaker opens when no envelope is waiting.
precise: a boot ROM function, selected by pins, fuses or the absence of a valid image, that receives code over USB or serial (Allwinner FEL, NXP serial download, Rockchip mask-ROM mode).
source: D9 of F4-32 (Vendor and community boot ROM documentation named in curriculum 11.2 and 11.4 (tier 3): the linux-sunxi community wiki on FEL, NXP's serial download protocol and Universal Update Utility (uuu), Rockchip's mask-ROM mode documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Arm's certification that a computer will boot ordinary, unmodified operating-system images.
analogy: the county's school inspection checklist.
precise: Arm's compliance programme combining hardware requirements (BSA, SBSA), firmware requirements (BBR, which includes EBBR for devicetree systems) and test suites (ACS); a certified system boots generic OS images through UEFI. Arm has reorganised its bands over time; read the current requirements document for today's names.
source: D3 of F4-33 (Arm, "Arm SystemReady Requirements Specification" and "Arm Base Boot Requirements (BBR)" (tier 1): bands, firmware requirements, ACS) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rules a small Arm or RISC-V board's firmware follows so that a standard OS can boot on it.
analogy: the short version of the inspection checklist for small schools.
precise: an open specification maintained by Arm and the community that defines the subset of UEFI that embedded firmware (U-Boot or EDK II) must provide and where the devicetree comes from (the UEFI configuration table).
source: D2 of F4-33 (Arm and community, "Embedded Base Boot Requirements (EBBR) Specification" (tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the minimum hardware an Arm system must have for a generic OS: a standard interrupt controller, timer, UART and so on.
analogy: the part of the checklist about the building itself: fire doors, a staff room.
precise: Arm's Base System Architecture and Server Base System Architecture specifications: required GIC version and behaviour, generic timer, watchdog, UART, PCIe behaviour and more.
source: D4 of F4-33 (Arm, "Arm Base System Architecture (BSA)" and "Arm Server Base System Architecture (SBSA)" (tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 128-bit number used as a name that nobody else will pick by accident.
analogy: a label printed by the county, not handwritten by each school.
precise: a globally unique identifier stored by UEFI as a 32-bit, two 16-bit and eight 8-bit fields; the first three are little-endian in memory and printed most significant digit first, the last eight are bytes in order.
source: D1 of F4-33 (UEFI Forum, "Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI) Specification" (tier 1): EFI System Table, EFI Configuration Table and its standard GUIDs (ACPI 2.0, SMBIOS 3, devicetree), Boot Services (GetMemoryMap, AllocatePool, ExitBootServices), memory types, the AArch64 calling convention and image type, the removable-media boot path) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the starting point of ACPI and the list of all other ACPI tables.
analogy: the index card that says where the folders are, and the list of folders.
precise: the Root System Description Pointer (signature "RSD PTR ", revision 2 or later for ACPI 2.0+) holds the 64-bit address of the Extended System Description Table, whose body is an array of 64-bit pointers to tables, each beginning with a four-character signature.
source: D5 of F4-33 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (tier 1): RSDP, XSDT, FADT, MADT, GTDT, PPTT, MCFG, SPCR, DBG2 and IORT (some of these defined in companion documents referenced by the specification)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one operating-system file set that boots on many different boards without being rebuilt.
analogy: the supply teacher who starts at nine in any school.
precise: an OS installation medium with a UEFI loader at the removable-media default path and no board-specific code selected at build time; hardware is learned at run time from ACPI or a devicetree passed through UEFI.
source: C1 of F4-33 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 11.3 "Arm SystemReady, EBBR and why they make 'any Arm board' easier", 11.4, and milestone D10 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html): the problem statement, the band history, the consequence for your loader, and the D10 build step and acceptance test quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a group of chips from one vendor that share a design, documentation style and boot method.
analogy: schools run by the same trust, with the same handbook layout.
precise: a vendor's line of SoCs (for example Rockchip RK33xx/RK35xx, NXP i.MX 8M) that share the boot ROM design, IP blocks, vendor tools and the shape of their TRMs and Linux support.
source: C1 of F4-34 (Systems Curriculum (this project), sections 11.4 "Platform families: boot chain and open documentation" and 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist", and milestones D8 and D10 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html): the family table, the checklist, and the D8 board test and D10 goal quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: drivers for a chip that are in the official versions of Linux or U-Boot, not only in a vendor's own copy.
analogy: the school's procedures published in the county handbook, not in a private folder.
precise: support merged into the upstream repositories (Linux, U-Boot, TF-A), maintained and reviewed there; contrasted with vendor ("downstream") trees that may be old, unreviewed or never merged.
source: C1 of F4-34 (Systems Curriculum (this project), sections 11.4 "Platform families: boot chain and open documentation" and 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist", and milestones D8 and D10 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html): the family table, the checklist, and the D8 board test and D10 goal quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a piece of firmware you must use but cannot read the source of.
analogy: a sealed envelope you must deliver without opening.
precise: vendor-supplied executable code without source (for example DRAM training, device-management or security firmware) that is loaded in the boot chain or by a driver; it limits what you can audit, change or fix.
source: C1 of F4-34 (Systems Curriculum (this project), sections 11.4 "Platform families: boot chain and open documentation" and 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist", and milestones D8 and D10 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html): the family table, the checklist, and the D8 board test and D10 goal quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a board whose chip only runs early boot code signed by the vendor, so you cannot replace it.
analogy: a school where only the trust's own staff may open the building in the morning.
precise: a boot ROM configured by one-time-programmable fuses to verify the first stage's signature against a vendor key; on such devices your code can run only as a payload of the vendor's later stages, if at all.
source: C1 of F4-34 (Systems Curriculum (this project), sections 11.4 "Platform families: boot chain and open documentation" and 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist", and milestones D8 and D10 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html): the family table, the checklist, and the D8 board test and D10 goal quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the wiring diagram of a board: what is connected to which pin.
analogy: the plumbing and wiring plan of the building.
precise: the circuit diagram of the board, showing the SoC's pin assignments, the debug UART connector and its voltage, boot-mode straps, regulators, and which peripherals are fitted; the board-level complement to the SoC's TRM.
source: C1 of F4-34 (Systems Curriculum (this project), sections 11.4 "Platform families: boot chain and open documentation" and 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist", and milestones D8 and D10 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html): the family table, the checklist, and the D8 board test and D10 goal quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a written list of what you will do, in which order, to make a new board run your code, and what you still need to find out.
analogy: the plan for the first week at a new school, written before the first day.
precise: a document that records the board's documentation set, the console and recovery procedure, the reference boot, the devicetree reading, the bring-up order of curriculum 11.5, the acceptance test for each step and the open questions.
source: C1 of F4-34 (Systems Curriculum (this project), sections 11.4 "Platform families: boot chain and open documentation" and 11.5 "SoC bring-up checklist", and milestones D8 and D10 in 11.6 (local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html): the family table, the checklist, and the D8 board test and D10 goal quoted verbatim) — a map, not a source (AH-4); pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: putting off a device's start-up until the things it depends on are ready, and trying again later.
analogy: the timetable postpones a lesson until the room is ready.
precise: a probe result meaning "a provider I need (clock, reset, interrupt controller, pin controller, regulator) has not been probed yet"; the driver model keeps the device waiting and retries after other probes succeed, stopping when a full pass makes no progress.
source: D3 of F4-35 (The Linux kernel documentation (tier 2), the driver model ("Device drivers infrastructure", deferred probing, device links) and "The Common Clk Framework" (curriculum item 119)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a clock controller hands out clocks; a device that needs one says which, in the devicetree.
analogy: the light switches of a wing, and the note on a room's door saying which switch it needs.
precise: a provider node has #clock-cells; a consumer's clocks property is a list of (phandle, n specifier cells) entries, with n taken from the provider, optionally named by clock-names.
source: D1 of F4-35 (devicetree.org, "Devicetree Specification" (tier 1): compatible, status, phandles, interrupt-parent and its inheritance, interrupt specifiers) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the block that holds other blocks in their starting state until software lets them go.
analogy: the locked door of a room.
precise: a provider with #reset-cells whose lines hold blocks in reset; a consumer's resets property names the line to release (and optionally reset-names).
source: D2 of F4-35 (The Linux kernel documentation (tier 2), devicetree bindings for clocks (#clock-cells, clocks, clock-names), resets (#reset-cells, resets, reset-names), pin control and GPIO, and the dt-schema tools (curriculum reading list item 95)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: choosing which of several jobs a chip's pin does, for example GPIO, UART or SD card.
analogy: arranging the furniture of a room for this lesson, not the last one.
precise: per-pin function-select registers in a pin controller, set by the OS (or firmware) according to pin configuration properties referenced from the consumer's node; Linux uses pinctrl-0 and pinctrl-names with vendor-specific child nodes.
source: D2 of F4-35 (The Linux kernel documentation (tier 2), devicetree bindings for clocks (#clock-cells, clocks, clock-names), resets (#reset-cells, resets, reset-names), pin control and GPIO, and the dt-schema tools (curriculum reading list item 95)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a list of drivers that the build tools assemble automatically from every driver file.
analogy: each interpreter signs a sheet on arrival; the office reads the sheet.
precise: each driver places a descriptor in a named section with __attribute__((used, section(...))); the linker script collects the section and defines start and end symbols, so the driver core needs no central list.
source: D4 of F4-35 (GNU Binutils, "LD" manual (tier 2): KEEP, output section symbols, and GCC's manual for the section and used attributes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a standard set of registers for the chip-side controller that talks to SD cards.
analogy: the office counter with a fixed form for talking to visitors.
precise: the SD Association's standard register interface for SD host controllers (argument, command, response, present state, host and power control, clock control, interrupt status, buffer data port, capabilities, version), implemented with quirks by many SoC vendors.
source: D2 of F4-36 (SD Association, "SD Specifications Part A2: SD Host Controller Simplified Specification" (tier 1): register map, command register encoding, response storage, present state, clock control, software reset, interrupt status, ADMA2) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a numbered request sent to the card, and the card's reply.
analogy: a numbered phrase from the phrasebook and the visitor's answer.
precise: a 48-bit command token (index CMD0–CMD63 plus a 32-bit argument) on the CMD line; responses are 48 bits (R1, R3, R6, R7) or 136 bits (R2); application commands (ACMDn) are preceded by CMD55.
source: D1 of F4-36 (SD Association, "SD Specifications Part 1: Physical Layer Simplified Specification" (tier 1): card initialisation, CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3, CMD7, CMD9, CMD16, CMD17, CMD24, OCR (CCS, busy), CID, CSD versions 1.0 and 2.0, addressing, identification clock, UHS voltage switching) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: four things the card tells you about itself: its voltage and readiness, its identity, its size and timing, and the short address you give it.
analogy: "I am ready", the visitor's name card, the size of her box, her desk number.
precise: Operation Conditions Register (voltage window, busy bit 31, Card Capacity Status bit 30), Card Identification register (manufacturer, product name, serial), Card-Specific Data (structure version, capacity fields), Relative Card Address (16 bits, published by the card in reply to CMD3).
source: D1 of F4-36 (SD Association, "SD Specifications Part 1: Physical Layer Simplified Specification" (tier 1): card initialisation, CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3, CMD7, CMD9, CMD16, CMD17, CMD24, OCR (CCS, busy), CID, CSD versions 1.0 and 2.0, addressing, identification clock, UHS voltage switching) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: older small cards are addressed in bytes; newer large cards are addressed in 512-byte blocks.
analogy: files asked for by distance from the front of the box, or by their number.
precise: for Standard Capacity cards (CCS = 0) the data command argument is a byte address; for High and Extended Capacity cards (CCS = 1 in the OCR) it is a block number; the driver must read CCS after initialisation and choose.
source: D1 of F4-36 (SD Association, "SD Specifications Part 1: Physical Layer Simplified Specification" (tier 1): card initialisation, CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, CMD3, CMD7, CMD9, CMD16, CMD17, CMD24, OCR (CCS, busy), CID, CSD versions 1.0 and 2.0, addressing, identification clock, UHS voltage switching) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an SD-like storage chip soldered onto the board, with its own version of the protocol.
analogy: a visitor who lives in the building and speaks a dialect of the same phrasebook.
precise: embedded MultiMediaCard, specified by JEDEC (JESD84 series): an MMC-protocol device with a controller, hardware partitions (boot areas, RPMB, user area) and an extended CSD register; it shares SDHCI host controllers with SD but initialises differently.
source: D3 of F4-36 (JEDEC, "Embedded Multi-Media Card (e•MMC) Electrical Standard" (JESD84 series) (tier 1): MMC initialisation, Extended CSD, CMD6, partitions) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one kernel file that runs on many boards, because it finds out what board it is on while it boots.
analogy: the teacher's one lesson book.
precise: a kernel binary with no compile-time board selection: load address, exception level, memory, CPUs, devices and firmware services are discovered from the boot protocol and from firmware tables (devicetree or ACPI), and devices are handled by drivers matched at run time.
source: D1 of F4-37 (The Linux kernel documentation, "Booting AArch64 Linux" (Documentation/arch/arm64/booting.rst) (tier 2): image header, text offset, x0 = DTB, MMU off, entry at EL2 or EL1, cache state) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that works wherever in memory it is loaded, because it fixes its own addresses first.
analogy: a book whose page references say "three pages on" instead of "page 47".
precise: code built with -fpie and linked with -pie: instructions address relative to the program counter, and every absolute pointer in data has an R_AARCH64_RELATIVE dynamic relocation that start-up code applies by adding the load address.
source: D5 of F4-37 (Arm, "ELF for the Arm 64-bit Architecture (AArch64)" (tier 1): R_AARCH64_RELATIVE, Elf64_Rela) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a note in the file saying "this word must be increased by wherever the file ends up".
analogy: a sticky note on page 12: "add the room number to this".
precise: an Elf64_Rela entry (offset, info, addend; 24 bytes) of type 1027, meaning: store load address + addend at load address + offset.
source: D5 of F4-37 (Arm, "ELF for the Arm 64-bit Architecture (AArch64)" (tier 1): R_AARCH64_RELATIVE, Elf64_Rela) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the same register can have one number seen from the SoC's internal bus and another seen from the processor.
analogy: a room called "B12" by the building plan and "the third door upstairs" by the staff.
precise: on SoCs whose peripherals hang on a bus with its own address map, the devicetree describes nodes in bus addresses and gives the translation in the parent's ranges; on QEMU's raspi3b, bus 0x7e000000 is CPU 0x3f000000.
source: D4 of F4-37 (devicetree.org, "Devicetree Specification" (tier 1): ranges, /chosen, stdout-path, memory and CPU nodes, enable-method) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
